description:
Two tests in tests/unit/scripts/test_remote_closeout.py fail on unmodified develop when the shell running pytest has `LANG=C` (the omp agent harness default): `test_the_reviewer_runs_isolated_from_user_config_secrets_and_the_network` and `test_claude_is_confined_to_read_only_tools_and_an_isolated_login`. Each asserts the reviewer's environment keys are exactly {PATH, HOME, LANG} (plus CODEX_HOME for the Codex case), minus `__CF_USER_TEXT_ENCODING`, and finds an extra `LC_CTYPE`.

Cause, observed 2026-11-17: `scripts/remote_review.py` passes the caller's LANG to the reviewer (`os.environ.get("LANG", "C.UTF-8")`, two call sites). The fake reviewers in the test are Python scripts that dump `dict(os.environ)` to env.json. With LANG=C, Python's locale coercion (PEP 538) sets `LC_CTYPE=UTF-8` in the fake's own environment at start-up, so the dump shows a variable the launcher never passed. With `LANG=en_US.UTF-8` or LANG unset, both tests pass; `env -u LC_CTYPE` does not help. Impact: `make pr-preflight` fails for every branch whose changes select these tests (anything importing pr_arm, pr_landing or remote_review) when run from a LANG=C shell, which pushes agents toward known-failures entries or ad-hoc LANG overrides.

Decision gate (implementer decides, records why here):
(a) start the fakes with `PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE=0` so they report exactly what the launcher passed (recommended: keeps the assertion exact and tests the launcher, not the interpreter);
(b) have the fake drop variables the interpreter adds, as it already drops `__CF_USER_TEXT_ENCODING`;
(c) change the launcher's LANG handling. Choose (c) only if the reviewer is shown to misbehave under LANG=C; that is a security-relevant change to an isolation allowlist and needs its own justification.

Guardrails: the reviewer environment stays an explicit allowlist and the assertions stay exact equality; no known-failures entry, skip or xfail; no change to which variables the launcher passes unless option (c) is chosen with the evidence above.
